The company needs a solution that will generate an email alert when an unencrypted DB instance or DB cluster is created. The solution also must terminate the unencrypted DB instance or DB cluster. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient manner?

options.A: Create an AWS Config managed rule to detect unencrypted RDS storage. Configure an automatic remediation action to publish messages to an Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) topic that includes an AWS Lambda function and an email delivery target as subscribers. Configure the Lambda function to delete the unencrypted resource
options.B: Create an AWS Config managed rule to detect unencrypted RDS storage. Configure a manual remediation action to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to publish messages to an Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) topicand to delete the unencrypted resource.
options.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that evaluates RDS event patterns and is initiated by the creation of DB instances or DB clusters. Configure the rule to publish messages to an Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) topic that includes an AWS Lambda function and an email delivery target as subscribers. Configure the Lambda function to delete the unencrypted resource.
options.D: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that evaluates RDS event patterns and is initiated by the creation of DB instances or DB clusters. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to publish messages to an Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) topicand to delete the unencrypted resource.

explanations.A: Correct. An AWS Config managed rule detects unencrypted RDS storage, and an automatic remediation action that publishes to an SNS topic (with an email subscriber and a Lambda function that deletes the resource) both alerts and terminates the unencrypted resource with the least operational effort.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A manual remediation action requires human initiation, so it is less operationally efficient than automatic remediation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Building an EventBridge rule on RDS event patterns to detect unencrypted storage is more custom work and less reliable than the AWS Config managed rule for encryption compliance.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This EventBridge-based approach is more custom to build and maintain than the AWS Config managed rule with automatic remediation.

question: A security engineer wants to evaluate configuration changes to a specific AWS resource to ensure that the resource meets compliance standards. However, the security engineer is concerned about a situation in which several configuration changes are made to the resource in quick succession. The security engineer wants to record only the latest configuration of that resource to indicate the cumulative impact of the set of changes. Which solution will meet this requirement in the MOST operationally efficient way?

options.A: Use AWS CloudTrail to detect the configuration changes by filtering API calls to monitor the changes. Use the most recent API call to indicate the cumulative impact of multiple calls.
options.B: Use AWS Config to detect the configuration changes and to record the latest configuration in case of multiple configuration changes.
options.C: Use Amazon CloudWatch to detect the configuration changes by filtering API calls to monitor the changes. Use the most recent API call to indicate the cumulative impact of multiple calls.
options.D: Use AWS Cloud Map to detect the configuration changes. Generate a report of configuration changes from AWS Cloud Map to track the latest state by using a sliding time window

explanations.A: Incorrect. CloudTrail records individual API calls, not the resulting cumulative resource configuration state, so it does not record the latest configuration item.
explanations.B: Correct. AWS Config records configuration items for resources and, when multiple changes occur in quick succession, records the latest configuration to reflect the cumulative impact, with minimal operational effort.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Amazon CloudWatch monitors metrics and can filter logs of API calls, but it does not record a resource's cumulative configuration state.
explanations.D: Incorrect. AWS Cloud Map is a service discovery tool; it does not track or record resource configuration changes.

question: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage an organization that consists of three workload OUs. Production, Development, and Testing. The company uses AWS CloudFormation templates to define and deploy workload infrastructure in AWS accounts that are associated with the OUs. Different SCPs are attached to each workload OU. The company successfully deployed a CloudFormation stack update to workloads in the Development OU and the Testing OU. When the company uses the same CloudFormation template to deploy the stack update in.an account in the Production OU, the update fails. The error message reports insufficient IAM permissions. What is the FIRST step that a security engineer should take to troubleshoot this issue?

options.A: Review the AWS CloudTrail logs in the account in the Production OU. Search for any failed API calls from CloudFormation during the deployment attempt.
options.B: Remove all the SCPs that are attached to the Production OU. Rerun the CloudFormation stack update to determine if the SCPs were preventing the CloudFormation API calls.
options.C: Confirm that the role used by CloudFormation has sufficient permissions to create, update, and delete the resources that are referenced in the CloudFormation template.
options.D: Make all the SCPs that are attached to the Production OU the same as the SCPs that are attached to the Testing OU.

explanations.A: Correct. Reviewing the CloudTrail logs in the Production OU account to find the failed CloudFormation API calls is the first step, because it pinpoints exactly which action was denied and whether an SCP or a missing IAM permission caused the insufficient-permissions error.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Removing all SCPs from the Production OU is risky and overly broad; you should first identify the failing API call in the logs rather than stripping guardrails.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Confirming the CloudFormation role's permissions is a valid later step, but the first step is to review the CloudTrail logs to determine exactly which API call failed and why.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Changing the Production OU's SCPs to match the Testing OU weakens production controls and assumes SCPs are the cause before investigating the actual failed API call.

question: A company hosts a web-based application that captures and stores sensitive data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company needs to implement a solution that provides end-to-end data protection and the ability to detect unauthorized datachanges. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use an AWS Key Management Service AWS KMS) customer managed key. Encrypt the data at rest.
options.B: Use AWS Private Certificate Authority. Encrypt the data in transit.
options.C: Use the DynamoDB Encryption Client. Use client-side encryption. Sign the table items.
options.D: Use the AWS Encryption SDK. Use client-side encryption. Sign the table items.

explanations.A: Incorrect. A KMS customer managed key encrypts data at rest but does not provide end-to-end client-side protection or the ability to detect unauthorized changes to individual items.
explanations.B: Incorrect. AWS Private CA and TLS encrypt data in transit only; they do not provide end-to-end protection at rest or detect tampering with items.
explanations.C: Correct. The DynamoDB Encryption Client performs client-side encryption for end-to-end protection and can sign table items so that unauthorized changes to the items can be detected.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The AWS Encryption SDK provides client-side encryption but is not integrated with DynamoDB item structure and does not natively sign DynamoDB table items the way the DynamoDB Encryption Client does.

question: A security engineer has created an Amazon GuardDuty detector in several AWS accounts. The accounts are in an organization in AWS Organizations. The security engineer needs centralized visibility of the security findings from the detectors. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.A: Configure Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights.
options.B: Create an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard.
options.C: Configure AWS Security Hub integrations.
options.D: Query the findings by using Amazon Athena.

explanations.A: Incorrect. CloudWatch Logs Insights queries log data; it does not provide centralized aggregation of GuardDuty findings across accounts.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A CloudWatch dashboard visualizes metrics; it does not centrally aggregate GuardDuty security findings.
explanations.C: Correct. AWS Security Hub integrates with GuardDuty and aggregates findings from multiple accounts, providing the centralized visibility required.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Querying findings with Athena requires exporting data and building custom queries; it is not the native centralized-visibility solution that Security Hub provides.

question: A company runs workloads on Amazon EC2 instances in VPCs. The EC2 instances make requests to Amazon S3 buckets through VPC endpoints. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage its AWS accounts. The company needs the requests from the EC2 instances to originate from the same VPC that the EC2 instance credentials were issued to. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.A: Deploy an SCP that includes the S3 action with the “aws:SourceVpc”: “${aws:Ec2InstanceSourceVpc}” condition.
options.B: Edit the VPC endpoints to include the S3 action with the “aws:Ec2InstanceSourcePrivateIPv4”: “${aws:VpcSourceIp}” condition.
options.C: Limit all actions in the S3 bucket policies by using the aws:SourceVpce condition key with the value of the allowed VPC endpoint.
options.D: Limit all actions in the S3 bucket policies by using the aws:SourceVpc condition key with the value of the allowed VPC ID.

explanations.A: Incorrect. An SCP is a guardrail on principals and the self-referential condition as written is not the correct mechanism to ensure S3 requests originate from the same VPC that issued the instance credentials.
explanations.B: Incorrect. VPC endpoint policies do not use an aws:Ec2InstanceSourcePrivateIPv4 to aws:VpcSourceIp mapping in this way, and this does not enforce that requests originate from the same VPC the credentials were issued to.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The aws:SourceVpce condition key restricts access to a specific VPC endpoint, not to the specific VPC that issued the instance credentials, so it does not meet the requirement.
explanations.D: Correct. Restricting the S3 bucket policy actions with the aws:SourceVpc condition key set to the allowed VPC ID ensures requests come from that VPC, matching the VPC to which the EC2 instance credentials were issued.

question: A company uses Amazon Cognito for external user authentication for a web application.External users report that they can no longer log in to the application. What is the FIRST step that a security engineer should take to troubleshoot the problem?

options.A: Review AWS CloudTrail logs to identify authentication errors that relate to Cognito users.
options.B: Use AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer to delete all unused IAM roles and users.
options.C: Review any recent changes in Cognito configuration, IAM policies, and role trust policies to identify issues.
options.D: Write a script that uses CLI commands to reset all user passwords in the Cognito user pool.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Reviewing CloudTrail logs can help later, but the first step is to check for recent configuration changes that broke authentication.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Deleting unused IAM roles and users with Access Analyzer is unrelated to the login failure and could cause further problems.
explanations.C: Correct. The first step is to review recent changes to the Cognito configuration, IAM policies, and role trust policies, because a recent misconfiguration is the most likely cause of users suddenly being unable to log in.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Resetting all user passwords is disruptive and does not address the likely root cause, which is a configuration change.

question: A company is running its application on AWS. Malicious users exploited a recent promotion event and created many fake accounts. The application currently uses Amazon CloudFront in front of an Amazon API Gateway API. AWS Lambda functions serve the different API endpoints. The GET registration endpoint is behind the path of /store/registration. The URI for submission of the new account details is at /store/newaccount. A security engineer needs to design a solution that prevents similar exploitations for future promotion events. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? Choose two.)

options.A: Create an AWS WAF web ACL. Add the AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet rule group to the web ACL. Associate the web ACL with the CloudFront distribution.
options.B: Create an AWS WAF web ACL. Add a rate limit rule to the web ACL. Include a RateBasedStatement entry that has a SearchString value that points to /store/registration.
options.C: Specify /store/registration as the registration page path. Specify /store/newaccount as the account creation path.
options.D: Enable AWS Shield Advanced for the account that hosts the CloudFront distribution. Configure a DNS-specific custom.
options.E: Enable Amazon GuardDuty for the account that hosts the CloudFront distribution. Enable Lambda Protection for the Lambda functions that answer calls to /store/registration and /store/newaccount.

explanations.A: Correct. Adding the AWS WAF account creation fraud prevention managed rule group (AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet) to a web ACL associated with the CloudFront distribution helps detect and block fraudulent account creation.
explanations.B: Correct. A rate-based rule in the web ACL that targets the /store/registration path limits high-volume automated requests to the registration endpoint, reducing mass fake-account creation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Simply specifying the registration and account-creation paths is a configuration input for other rules, not a protective control by itself.
explanations.D: Incorrect. AWS Shield Advanced protects against DDoS attacks; it does not prevent fraudulent account creation, and the described DNS configuration is not relevant.
explanations.E: Incorrect. GuardDuty Lambda Protection detects threats to Lambda functions; it does not prevent fake account creation at the application layer.

question: A company is investigating an increase in its AWS monthly bill. The company discovers that bad actors compromised some Amazon EC2 instances and served webpages for a large email phishing campaign. A security engineer must implement a solution to monitor for cost increases in the future to help detect malicious activity. Which solution will offer the company the EARLIEST detection of cost increases?

options.A: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function hourly. Program the Lambda function to download an AWS usage report from AWS Data Exports about usage of all services. Program the Lambda function to analyze the report and to send a notification when anomalies are detected.
options.B: Create a cost monitor in AWS Cost Anomaly Detection. Configure an individual alert to notify an Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) topic when the percentage above the expected cost exceeds a threshold.
options.C: Review AWS Cost Explorer daily to detect anomalies in cost from prior months. Review the usage of any services that experience a significant cost increase from prior months.
options.D: Capture VPC flow logs from the VPC where the EC2 instances run. Use a third-party network analysis tool to analyze the flow logs and to detect anomalies in network traffic that might increase cost.

explanations.A: Incorrect. An hourly Lambda that downloads and analyzes usage reports is custom, delayed by report availability, and less timely than AWS Cost Anomaly Detection.
explanations.B: Correct. AWS Cost Anomaly Detection continuously monitors spend using machine learning and can alert an SNS topic when costs exceed the expected threshold, providing the earliest detection of cost increases.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Manually reviewing Cost Explorer daily is slow and reactive, so it does not provide the earliest detection.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Analyzing VPC flow logs with a third-party tool detects network anomalies, not cost increases directly, and is more complex.

question: A company ʼ s network security policy requires encryption for all data in transit. The company must encrypt data that is sent between Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon Elastic Block Store Amazon EBS) volumes. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.A: Configure Amazon EC2 to enable encryption in the EC2 network interface properties.
options.B: Configure Amazon EBS to enable volume encryption with AWS Key Management Service AWS KMS) for data at rest.
options.C: Configure Amazon EBS to enable TLS encryption in the volume configuration properties.
options.D: Configure Amazon EC2 to enable TLS encryption with certificates that are stored in AWS Certificate Manager ACM .

explanations.A: Incorrect. There is no EC2 network interface property that encrypts traffic between an instance and its EBS volumes.
explanations.B: Incorrect. EBS volume encryption with KMS protects data at rest, not data in transit as required.
explanations.C: Incorrect. There is no TLS encryption setting in EBS volume configuration properties for in-transit encryption between EC2 and EBS.
explanations.D: Correct. Configuring EC2 to use TLS encryption with certificates managed in AWS Certificate Manager encrypts the data in transit, meeting the requirement.

question: A company runs a web application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances that are in an Auto Scaling group. The EC2 instances are in the same VPC subnet as other workloads. A security engineer deploys an Amazon GuardDuty detector in the same AWS Region as the EC2 instances. The security engineer also sets up an AWS Security Hub integration with GuardDuty. The security engineer needs to implement an automated solution to detect and appropriately respond to anomalous traffic patterns for the web application. The solution must comply with AWS best practices for initial response to security incidents and must minimize disruption to the web application. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that detects the Behavior:EC2/TrafficVolumeUnusual GuardDuty finding. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to disable the EC2 instance profile access keys.
options.B: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function when GuardDuty detects anomalous traffic. Program the Lambda function to disassociate the identified instance from the Auto Scaling group and to isolate the instance by using a new restricted security group.
options.C: Create a Security Hub automated response that updates the network ACL that is associated with the subnet of the EC2 instances. Configure the response to update the network ACL to deny traffic from the source of detected anomalous traffic.
options.D: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the security engineer ʼ s email address to the SNS topic. Configure GuardDuty to send all findings to the SNS topic.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Disabling the EC2 instance profile access keys does not isolate anomalous network traffic and does not properly contain the affected instance.
explanations.B: Correct. An EventBridge rule that invokes a Lambda function to disassociate the instance from the Auto Scaling group and isolate it with a restricted security group contains the affected instance per incident-response best practices while minimizing disruption to the running application.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Updating the subnet's network ACL to deny the source affects all instances in the subnet, including healthy workloads, which does not minimize disruption.

question: A company has an application that needs to read objects from an Amazon S3 bucket. The company configures an IAM policy and attaches the policy to an IAM role that the application uses. When the application tries to read objects from the S3 bucket, the application receives AccessDenied errors. A security engineer must resolve this problem without decreasing the security of the S3 bucket or the application. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to grant read access to the role.
options.B: Launch a new deployment of the application in a different AWS Region. Attach the role to the application.
options.C: Review the IAM policy by using AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer to ensure that the policy grants the right permissions. Validate that the application is assuming the role correctly.
options.D: Ensure that the S3 Block Public Access feature is disabled on the S3 bucket. Review AWS CloudTrail logs to validate that the application is assuming the role correctly.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Adding a bucket resource policy to grant the role access broadens the bucket's access surface and may not address the root cause, which could be the IAM policy or role assumption.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Redeploying the application in a different Region does not resolve an IAM permissions or role-assumption problem.
explanations.C: Correct. Using IAM Access Analyzer to review the IAM policy confirms it grants the correct permissions, and validating that the application is correctly assuming the role resolves the AccessDenied error without reducing security.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Disabling S3 Block Public Access reduces the bucket's security and is unnecessary, because the application uses a role rather than public access.

question: A security engineer is designing a solution that will provide end-to-end encryption between clients and Docker containers running in Amazon Elastic Container Service Amazon ECS . This solution will also handle volatile traffic patterns. Which solution would have the MOST scalability and LOWEST latency?

options.A: Configure a Network Load Balancer to terminate the TLS traffic and then re-encrypt the traffic to the containers.
options.B: Configure an Application Load Balancer to terminate the TLS traffic and then re-encrypt the traffic to the containers.
options.C: Configure a Network Load Balancer with a TCP listener to pass through TLS traffic to the containers.
options.D: Configure Amazon Route 53 to use multivalue answer routing to send traffic to the containers.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Terminating TLS at a Network Load Balancer and re-encrypting to the containers adds processing overhead and does not provide true end-to-end encryption from client to container.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An Application Load Balancer terminates TLS, which breaks end-to-end encryption, and it operates at layer 7 with higher latency and less raw scalability than a passthrough NLB for this pattern.
explanations.C: Correct. A Network Load Balancer with a TCP listener passes the TLS traffic straight through to the containers, preserving end-to-end encryption while providing the highest scalability and lowest latency for volatile traffic.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Route 53 multivalue answer routing distributes traffic through DNS but does not provide load balancing scalability or the low-latency, end-to-end encrypted path that an NLB passthrough offers.

question: A company has a large fleet of Amazon Linux 2 Amazon EC2 instances that run an application. The application processes sensitive data and has the following compliance requirements: No remote access management ports to the EC2 instances can be exposed internally or externally. • All remote session activity must be recorded in an audit log. • All remote access to the EC2 instances must be authenticated and authorized by AWS IAM Identity Center. The company ʼ s DevOps team occasionally needs to connect to one of the EC2 instances to troubleshoot issues. Which solution will provide remote access to the EC2 instances while meeting the compliance requirements?

options.A: Grant access to the EC2 serial console at the account level. Create an IAM policy that allows an IAM role of the DevOps team to access the EC2 serial console.
options.B: Enable EC2 instance Connect on the AMI of the EC2 instances. Configure the appropriate security group rules. Grant EC2 console access to the DevOps team for access to EC2 instance Connect.
options.C: Assign an EC2 instance role that allows access to AWS Systems Manager. Create an IAM policy that grants access to Systems Manager Session Manager. Assign the policy to an IAM role of the DevOps team.
options.D: Use AWS Systems Manager Automation runbooks to open remote access ports to the EC2 instances. Attach a role to the EC2 instances to allow the runbooks to run.

explanations.A: Incorrect. EC2 serial console access is for low-level troubleshooting and does not record remote session activity in an audit log or authorize access through IAM Identity Center as required.
explanations.B: Incorrect. EC2 Instance Connect requires opening SSH (port 22) and configuring security group rules, which violates the requirement to expose no remote management ports.
explanations.C: Correct. AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, using an instance role and an IAM policy that grants Session Manager access, provides remote access without open ports, records all session activity in audit logs, and authenticates and authorizes access through IAM and IAM Identity Center.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Using Systems Manager Automation runbooks to open remote access ports directly violates the requirement that no remote management ports be exposed.
